# Check 5: hindcast cross-validation

The hindcast compares the observations of the peeled years with their one-year-ahead predictions from the
retrospective runs (Kell et al. 2016). The mean absolute scaled error (MASE) scales the prediction error by that
of a naive random-walk forecast: MASE < 1 means the model predicts better than the naive forecast. `ss3_hindcast()`
does indices, mean length and mean age, as `ss3diags::SSmase()`.

```{r hc}
data(retro.phk)
hc <- ss3_hindcast(retro.phk)
hc$mase
```

```{r hc-plot, fig.height = 4}
ss3plot_hcxval(hc)
```

```{r hc-sma, fig.height = 5}
ss3plot_hcxval(ss3_hindcast(retro.sma))
```

> **Check 5: prediction skill.** MASE > 1 for an index means the model has no prediction skill for it. With
> indices that vary little the naive error is small and `MAE.base.adj` (default 0.1) limits the scaling.

## All checks at a glance: the model scorecard

`ss3_scorecard()` collects the checks of this guide into one pass/fail table for one or more models:

- runs tests of the index residuals (p >= 0.05);
- retrospective and forecast Mohn's rho of SSB, within [-0.15, 0.2] for long-lived species (Hurtado-Ferro et al.
  2015; `rho = c(-0.22, 0.3)` for short-lived species);
- hindcast MASE of each index (< 1);
- the OSA tests of the compositions (`quant = "len"` or `"age"`).

Criteria a model cannot provide (e.g. without retrospective runs) are left grey. Here the mako shark and Pacific
hake models are side by side, to show the layout:

```{r scorecard}
sc <- ss3_scorecard(list(mako = ss3sma, `Pacific hake` = ss3phk), retro = list(mako = retro.sma, `Pacific hake` = retro.phk),
                    quant = "age", nsim = 199)
sc$table
```

```{r scorecard-plot, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 7}
ss3plot_scorecard(sc)
```

> **Using the scorecard.** The scorecard summarises; it does not decide. A model that fails one check is not
> necessarily worse than one that passes all, and the thresholds are conventions. For ensembles, the scorecard
> helps to justify which models enter and how they are weighted, but the weights should not be tuned to the advice.
